newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire troops urged to lay down arms in Lubumbashi.
newsitem.headline: Zaire troops urged to lay down arms in Lubumbashi.

text.p: Local radio in Zaire's second city Lubumbashi repeatedly broadcast an appeal to government troops on Monday, urging them to lay down their arms, refrain from looting and welcome advancing rebel forces as brothers.
Local residents said the broadcast appeal, in the Lingala language which most of the government troops speak, came from members of the army.

Normal life in Lubumbashi ground to a halt on Monday morning as reports came in from the border town of Kipushi, just 30 km (20 miles) down the road that a force of Laurent Kabila's rebel army was on its way.
Shops and businesses were closed and there were few taxis or people on the streets.

One businessman in Kipushi who watched the rebels sweep through the town before dawn estimated there were between 1,000 and 2,000 of them, but there was no confirmation of that figure, and no clear indication either of government troop numbers in Lubumbashi.
Scores of soldiers were moving around near their barracks in Lubumbashi as the radio appeal was repeated, talking among themselves.
